original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Lower bounds and reductions for the P104 centre (owned descent mass per FULL, 56 in the word) when centre contents are arbitrary vectors (not root-code), multi-generation descents allowed: a per-content ancestry bound (Lemma S), a Collapse theorem reducing every mixing-free centre to a Model C decoder, the resulting floors via the Model C results for #968's unit, and exact evidence on truncated and overcomplete contents.
scope_change_reason: The P104 centre is 56 per FULL; research/p104-multigen-centre-floor bounded it for root-code contents. This package removes the root-code hypothesis and locates exactly where a cheaper centre would have to live.
bottleneck_link: The owned centre is 56 units of the P104 word's paid mass per FULL; single-generation decoder floors cover it only for root-code factors or few terms, and no prior result priced multi-generation descents with arbitrary contents.
stop_rule: Stop after the Collapse theorem with its P104 consequences, exact controls on the existing designs and recorded evidence (truncation, overcomplete removed-root directions, frame counting); no proof attempt of Model C cases (b)-(d) beyond that.

open_questions.question: Can a step that mixes landed contents (or a landed content with first-generation material) ever lower the P104 centre below 56, with root-code or arbitrary contents?
open_questions.why_it_matters: By the Collapse theorem mixing is the only multi-generation mechanism not priced by Model C; every mixing-free centre costs at least its collapsed Model C decoder.
open_questions.first_step: In the R_8 = 0 pair-mix designs of PROOF.md section 7 (cost 52, four sign-mismatched ports unserved), single-port chains of total cost 3 are excluded (evidence/repair_shapes.py); decide whether three unit steps serving some port jointly (two steps, neither suiting it alone) can serve all four, which would be a 55 centre.
open_questions.blocked_by: Lemma S bounds each delivery by its own ancestry; shared ancestries need a joint potential.

open_questions.question: Is #968's P104 Model C case (c) at m = 9 (square decoder of a rank-9 realisation) at least 56, and is case (b) at m >= 10 in the shallow profiles (R_8 <= 5, or R_8 = 6 with R_7 <= 7) and case (d) at least 56?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A mixing-free centre below 56 must have its collapsed decoder in one of these classes, with at least nine pairwise non-proportional paid first-generation contents.
open_questions.first_step: Case (c): classify rank-9 realisations of the P104 pattern with the frame-module theorem of decoder-floors-frontier-format section 3.3 and price the dead sets of their dual bases.
open_questions.blocked_by: Frame incidence alone cannot prove 56 (landing frames inside removed hyperplanes meet more frames per unit cost than the frame-pair); the label-span structure must enter.

outcome_note: Any P104 centre of cost at most 55, whatever its contents, must either mix landed contents in an owned descent or have at least nine pairwise non-proportional paid first-generation contents whose collapsed Model C decoder lies in an open class (case (c) at m = 9, or a factor outside the column/row space at m >= 10). One-sided decoders (root-code columns, or by transposition root-code coefficients with arbitrary contents) cost at least 56 at every m in the deep profiles R_8 >= 7 or (R_8, R_7) = (6, 8). Truncated frame-pair contents break all 52 users, and in the overcomplete removed-root family the frame-pair is a strict local optimum. In the all-planes family, one mixed rotation replaces two pure ones for ten direction pairs up to one sign-mismatched port each; the matched designs cost 52 plus at least 4 standalone repair units, i.e. 56.
